key_insight: World from Motion turns a single monocular video into a freely renderable dynamic 3D Gaussian scene. It uses motion-aware conditioning to fix rendering artifacts and recover missing geometry/appearance from the initial reconstruction.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the difficulty of reconstructing high-quality, dynamic 3D scenes from only monocular video, especially when novel-view rendering suffers from holes, artifacts, and incomplete motion understanding.
method: Reconstruct an initial dynamic 3D Gaussian scene from monocular video.
Condition a video model on dense, pixel-aligned renderings that encode appearance, geometry, and 3D scene motion for both the input and target camera paths.
Use the model to correct rendering artifacts and hallucinate missing regions, producing a more complete and freely renderable dynamic 3D representation.
Train on a new dataset of aligned multiview video pairs and dynamic 3DGS representations.
impact: This makes monocular video-based 3D scene reconstruction more usable for view synthesis, AR/VR, robotics, and content creation. For practitioners, it improves render quality and completeness without requiring full multi-view capture.

paper_title: World from Motion: Generative Dynamic Gaussian Reconstruction from Monocular Video
paper_authors: Liyuan Zhu, Shengyu Huang, Amrita Mazumdar, Tianye Li, Zan Gojcic
